bandReport.notes: BOUNDARIES. Item 17 opens at the top of p10-c1 with its own number and is whole on my pages; I checked p08 (not my territory) to be sure nothing spilled forward - p08 ends with item 16 complete and carries NO directions block, so items 11-16 are standalone and nothing governs item 17. Item 26 ends with its option (d) on p16-c2 and is whole. || CROSS-BAND HAZARD, PLEASE READ. p12-c1 opens the block 'Directions for the following 7 (seven) items : Read the following five passages...', which governs items 21-27. Only 21-26 are printed on my pages; ITEM 27 IS ON p18 AND BELONGS TO THE NEXT BAND, but it is governed by Passage-5, which is printed on MY page 16 (it starts on p16-c1 under the heading 'Passage-5' and finishes on p16-c2). I confirmed on p18 that item 27 reads 'Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message of the passage?' and prints no passage of its own. So the p18 agent must reach BACK to p16 for Passage-5 or item 27 ships unanswerable. I have given item 26 the full Passage-5 text; if item 27 arrives without it, that is the seam, not a disagreement. || PASSAGE MAP for the 7-item block (five passages, seven items - the nesting the brief warns about): Passage-1 (private/foreign investment, FDI; p12-c1) governs item 21 ONLY. Passage-2 (monsoon flows and reservoirs; starts p12-c2, finishes at the top of p14-c1) governs item 22 ONLY. Passage-3 (economic freedom, tax rates and investment in education; starts p14-c1, finishes at the top of p14-c2) governs item 23 ONLY. Passage-4 (urban bodies, financing water delivery; starts p14-c2, finishes at the top of p16-c1) governs items 24 AND 25. Passage-5 (agriculture, structural transformation and poverty; starts p16-c1, finishes at the top of p16-c2) governs item 26 and, overleaf, item 27. Four of the five passages therefore span the column gutter or a page turn; each was read from the two column crops in c1-then-c2 order and its continuation confirmed against the whole-page image. || EXPECTED 'lonely context' WARNINGS. Items 21, 22 and 23 each have a context used by exactly one question. That is legitimate here, not per-item material parked in context: this single directions block genuinely gives those three items a passage each. Item 26's context will also look lonely until item 27 is merged in from the next band - see the cross-band note above. || STEM vs CONTEXT. Every numbered assumption/implication list (item 21's 1-5, item 22's 1-5, item 23's 1-3, item 25's 1-2, item 26's 1-4) is unique to its own item and is in the STEM, never in context - four of those items otherwise share the identical wording 'With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made ... Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?' and would collide on content_hash. Item 17's S1/S2 and 'Question :' lines are likewise in the stem for the same reason; its four options are the standard data-sufficiency boilerplate. The 'Directions for the following 7 (seven) items' preamble itself is NOT in any context field. || COLUMN CROPS. p10-c1, p10-c2, p12-c1, p12-c2 and p16-c1 are clean. p14-c2 and p16-c2 each carry a narrow vertical sliver of the neighbouring column's line-END letters down the left margin (on p14-c2: 'e', 're', 'st', 's', 'y'; on p16-c2: 'es', 'er', 'al', 'nt', 'of', 'ns'); no line of column 2 is cut and no text is lost, so this is the expected overlap, not a slice. p16 is the one page whose gutter was detected off the booklet's norm (_render.json gives gutterX 773 against 824-827 on my other three pages, a 53px shift), which is why its c2 sliver is the widest and why its c1 footer shows the page number '17' clipped to '1'. That clipping is page chrome only - I checked every line of p16-c1 against p16.png and no question text is missing from the right edge of that crop. || TYPOGRAPHY, transcribed as printed. This booklet sets the decimal point as a raised middle dot, so item 18's table and options read '8·8', '7·8', '7·6', '7·4', '7·2' and Passage-5 reads '4·1%' and '2·4%'. Kept verbatim per section 4. Passage-5's year ranges use en-dashes (1988–2014, 2005–2012, 2013–2014) and it carries one em-dash ('dramatically—almost'); both kept as printed. Curly apostrophes are transcribed as straight ASCII apostrophes throughout to keep the JSON encoding-safe - no wording is changed. Item 26's statement 1 is hyphenated across a line break in print ('transforma-tion') and is transcribed as the single word 'transformation'. Item 18's table is a genuine printed grid and is written as a GFM pipe table with its separator row; its top-left header cell is blank in the booklet and is left blank. The italic 'x' in that table and in item 18's question line is the only mathematical symbol in my band and is wrapped as \(x\). || DEFECTS. None found. No duplicate option text, no missing or blank option, no skipped item number, and no item I could not read. There is no answer key in this booklet and I have supplied no answers.

questions.stem:
Two Statements S1 and S2 are given below followed by a Question :
S1 : There are not more than two figures on any page of a 51-page book.
S2 : There is at least one figure on every page.
Question :
Are there more than 100 figures in that book?
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Statements and the Question?

options.label: A
options.text: Both S1 and S2 are sufficient to answer the Question, but neither S1 alone nor S2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question.

options.label: B
options.text: S1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question.

options.label: C
options.text: S1 and S2 together are not sufficient to answer the Question.

options.label: D
options.text: S2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question.

questions.subject: General Mental Ability

questions.context: Private investment in general is volatile. Foreign private investment is more volatile because the available investment avenues are significantly greater (i.e., the entire world). Therefore, the responsibility of providing employment cannot be left to Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). The current FDI inflows are volatile over time and across sectors and regions, which is a necessary consequence of their search for the highest returns. The adverse consequences are unstable employment and an accentuation of income and regional inequalities. A probable positive consequence of foreign investment is the inflow of new technology and its subsequent diffusion. However, the technology diffusion is not at all certain because the existing state of physical and human capital in India may prove inadequate for the diffusion.
questions.stem:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made :
1. Relying on foreign investment in the long run is not an economically sound policy.
2. Policies must be undertaken to reduce volatility in foreign private investment.
3. Policies must be undertaken to strengthen domestic private investment.
4. Public investment should be given priority over private investment.
5. Substantial public investment in education and health should be undertaken.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.subject: Comprehension

questions.context: Many opportunities to harness the highly skewed, seasonal and spatial distribution of monsoon flows, which occur in a four-month period from June to September annually, have been lost. Since these few months account for most of the rainfall and consequent freshwater availability, the need for holding rainwater in reservoirs, for subsequently releasing it for use over the year, is a necessity nobody can afford to overlook. Climate change will continue to affect weather conditions and create water shortages and excesses. While millions suffer from droughts and floods, waters in the country's many rivers flow unutilized, and are discharged into the sea every year.
questions.stem:
With reference to the above passage, which of the following could be the most rational and practical implications for India?
1. Inter-linking of rivers should be undertaken.
2. A network of dams and canals should be built across the country for proper distribution of water.
3. Farmers should be provided easy loans for digging borewells.
4. Usage of water for agriculture should be regulated by law.
5. Distribution of river water among regions should be regulated by the Union Government.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.subject: Comprehension

questions.context: People will invest in education whenever they are granted the economic freedom to fully enjoy its benefits. Again, this is for the obvious reason that the return on education increases as the level of economic freedom rises. When people, thanks to lower tax rates, are allowed to retain most of the higher income that they gain from each incremental level of education, it makes eminent sense to invest in education. On the other hand, when the government decides to tax the higher income of educated individuals at even higher rates, it makes very little sense to invest in educating oneself further. The same incentives apply to parents who decide on whether to invest in their children's education.
questions.stem:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made :
1. Lower tax rates in a country invariably translate into greater investments in higher education.
2. Investment in the education of children ensures their economic freedom.
3. Economic freedom has a positive impact on building up human capital.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?

questions.context: Our urban bodies cannot possibly ensure sustainable delivery of water in our cities unless financing mechanisms are put in place. Water delivery requires heavy investment in collecting it from a natural source, treating it to make it potable, and laying a distribution network of pipes for delivery to the users. It also requires investments in sewerage infrastructure and sewage treatment plants so that the sewers can carry the wastewater to these plants to ensure that no untreated sewage is discharged back into natural water bodies. If our cities were rich enough to meet the entire cost, water could be delivered free. They are not.
questions.stem: What is the most logical and crucial message conveyed by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Urban local bodies must recover costs through user charges.

options.label: B
options.text: Urban local bodies are not efficient enough to meet the water requirements of our cities.

options.label: C
options.text: Water shortage in our cities is a perennial problem that cannot be solved.

options.label: D
options.text: In view of the water crisis in our cities, there is an urgent need to limit the population of cities by adopting an upper limit of population size.

questions.context: In India, agriculture still engages about half of its workforce, and about 85 per cent of its farms are small and marginal. Compared to China and Vietnam, which have experienced fast structural and rural transformation, India's story is of slow transformation. As a result, poverty reduction in India was at a much slower pace during 1988–2014, compared to China and Vietnam. India's poverty reduction was slow during 1988–2005, but during 2005–2012, it accelerated dramatically—almost three times faster than during the earlier period. What did India do during this period? Research reveals that the relative price scenario changed significantly (by more than 50%) in favour of agriculture in the wake of rising global prices. This boosted private investments in agriculture by more than 50%. As a result, agri-GDP growth touched 4·1% during 2007–2012 as against 2·4% during 2002–2007. The net surplus of agri-trade touched $25 billion in 2013–2014; real farm wages rose by 7% per annum. All this led to unprecedented fall in poverty.
questions.stem:
With reference to the above passage, the following assumptions have been made :
1. Structural and rural transformation is impossible when farms are mainly small and marginal.
2. A good price incentive can trigger investments in agriculture.
3. India needs to build value chains for high-value agri-products like livestock and horticulture.
4. Higher global prices of agricultural commodities are essential for India's poverty reduction.
Which of the above assumptions are valid?
